title: The Promises and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence for Teachers: a Systematic Review of Research
authors: İsmail Çelik, Muhterem Dindar, Hanni Muukkonen, Sanna Järvelä
explain_beginner: This review looked at how teachers use artificial intelligence in their work. It found that AI can help teachers in three main ways. It can help them plan lessons by showing what students need. It can help during teaching by giving feedback right away. It can also help grade essays automatically. The review also found that teachers are not just users of AI. They help train it by acting as examples, and they check whether the automatic grading is correct. The paper also points out that using AI in teaching comes with challenges, so schools should think carefully before adopting it.
explain_business: This review suggests AI can support teachers with lesson planning, real time feedback, and automated essay scoring, which could ease workload pressures in these areas. It also shows that teachers remain essential to making these systems work, since they help train the algorithms and verify automated assessments. For leaders, the practical message is that AI adoption in classrooms is not purely a software purchase. It requires teacher time and involvement, plus attention to implementation challenges. This informs decisions about where to pilot AI, how to budget for staff involvement, and how to set realistic expectations for rollout.
explain_practitioner: This systematic review examined research on teachers' use of AI applications and machine learning methods for analyzing teacher data. The authors report that AI supports three areas of teaching: planning, by identifying and communicating student needs, implementation, through immediate feedback and enabling teacher intervention, and assessment, via automated essay scoring. The review also identifies teacher roles in AI development, including serving as models for training algorithms and verifying the accuracy of automated assessment systems. Several implementation challenges in teaching practice are highlighted, and the authors present these as guidelines for future work in the field.
